label: Nebulae
description: A separately loaded overlay of the catalogued nebulae within about 2000 ly, rendered as approximate 3D volumes. Large H II regions take their sky shape from an all-sky H-alpha map.

cutoffPolicy: Every reflection nebula, H II region and planetary nebula that is listed in NGC/IC, van den Bergh, van den Bergh & Herbst, Sharpless, HASH, or in Lynds with a reflection-catalogue identification (Cederblad or Dorschner & Gürtler), spans at least 5 arcmin, and whose adopted distance is within 1 sigma of 2000 ly (distance - error <= 613.2 pc); the census is being added in reviewed batches, so it is not yet complete beyond 500 ly (153.3 pc). Distances come from the SIMBAD-adopted parallax (Gaia EDR3, else Hipparcos 2007) of the illuminating or central star; several stars use an inverse-variance mean, and Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes or VLBA parallaxes of cluster members replace stars whose own parallax is unreliable or embedded. Sizes come from LBN for named NGC/IC nebulae, Sharpless for ionized nebulae, the SIMBAD-adopted angular diameter (or HASH radius) for planetary nebulae, twice the van den Bergh maximum radius in the north, and ESO/Uppsala or the van den Bergh & Herbst diameter south of the Lynds limit. H II regions larger than about 1 degree take their sky shape and relative brightness from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map. The Orion Nebula (about 1265 ly) was kept as a showcase beyond the earlier 500-ly cutoff. Excluded: dark nebulae and molecular clouds, nebulae under 5 arcmin, the possible planetary nebula FP J1912-0331, H-alpha-only ionized regions such as Spica's, and Barnard's Loop until its distance is settled (published estimates of about 170 and 440 pc disagree).
snapshot: J2000 map positions; literature reviewed 2026-10-01 (500-ly census), 2026-11-03 (2000-ly batch 1) and 2026-11-04 (batches 2 and 3).
